subject: FAR
title: ソフトウェアバンドル契約の収益配分と認識時期
scenario:
Apex Software Inc. は Year 1 の **7月1日**に、顧客と以下のバンドル契約（取引価格 **$80,000**・一括払い）を締結しました。契約には3つの独立した履行義務が含まれており、ASC 606 の5ステップモデルに基づいて収益認識を行う必要があります。

各履行義務の詳細は **Exhibit 1** を参照してください。

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: 契約の履行義務とスタンドアロン販売価格
exhibits.content:
| 履行義務 | スタンドアロン販売価格（SSP） | 引渡し時期・条件 |
|---|---|---|
| ソフトウェアライセンス | $60,000 | Year 1 7/1 に即時使用可能（時点での認識） |
| インストールサービス | $20,000 | Year 1 7/8 までに完了（時点での認識） |
| 1年間テクニカルサポート | $20,000 | Year 1 7/1 ～ Year 2 6/30（一定期間での認識） |
| **合計 SSP** | **$100,000** | |

**契約取引価格**: $80,000（割引あり）

tasks.title: ライセンスへの配分額
tasks.instruction: ASC 606 の相対的スタンドアロン販売価格（RSSV）法を用いて、**ソフトウェアライセンス**に配分される取引価格を計算してください（単位: ドル、端数なし）。
tasks.explanation: Allocation = $80,000 × ($60,000 / $100,000) = $48,000. The transaction price is allocated to each performance obligation in proportion to its standalone selling price.
tasks.explanationJa: 配分額 = $80,000 × ($60,000 / $100,000) = **$48,000**。取引価格は各履行義務のSSPの比率に応じて按分配分します（RSSV法）。

tasks.title: 1年間テクニカルサポートへの配分額
tasks.instruction: RSSV法を用いて、**1年間テクニカルサポート**に配分される取引価格を計算してください（単位: ドル、端数なし）。

tasks.title: Year 1 の収益認識合計
tasks.instruction: Year 1（1月1日 ～ 12月31日）に Apex Software が認識すべき収益合計を計算してください（単位: ドル、端数なし）。
tasks.explanation: License $48,000 (recognized 7/1) + Installation $16,000 (recognized by 7/8) + Support $16,000 × 6/12 = $8,000 (July 1 – December 31). Total = $72,000.

tasks.title: Year 1 末の繰延収益残高
tasks.instruction: Year 1 の貸借対照表（12月31日時点）に計上される**繰延収益**の金額を計算してください（単位: ドル、端数なし）。
tasks.explanation: The remaining support obligation: $16,000 × 6/12 = $8,000 (January 1 – June 30, Year 2 not yet earned).
tasks.explanationJa:
テクニカルサポートのうち Year 2 分（1〜6月）がまだ未履行のため、繰延収益として計上。

$16,000 × 6/12 = **$8,000**

subject: FAR
title: Variable Consideration and Sales with a Right of Return
scenario:
Crestline Tool & Supply Co. manufactures industrial fasteners and hand-tool products. The company prepares its financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP and recognizes revenue under ASC 606. Its fiscal year ends December 31.

During the first quarter of Year 1, Crestline entered into two separate arrangements:

1. A one-year master supply agreement with Bryce Manufacturing Corp. that includes a retroactive volume rebate. The contract terms are presented in **Exhibit 1**, and first-quarter delivery activity together with management's probability assessment of Bryce's annual purchase volume is presented in **Exhibit 2**.
2. March sales of Model X tool kits to independent distributors under a 60-day right of return. The March distributor sales data are presented in **Exhibit 3**.

Control of all products transfers to the customer upon delivery. Using the information in the exhibits, complete Work Tabs 1 through 7.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Master Supply Agreement (Excerpts) — Bryce Manufacturing Corp.
exhibits.content:
| Term | Detail |
|---|---|
| Contract period | January 1, Year 1 – December 31, Year 1 |
| Product | Grade-8 industrial fasteners |
| List price | $50 per unit, invoiced upon delivery |
| Payment terms | Net 30; past-due balances accrue interest at 1.5% per month |
| Shipping terms | FOB shipping point; freight paid by Bryce |
| Volume rebate | A retroactive rebate applies to **all** units purchased during the contract year, based on total annual volume, and is settled in cash in January of Year 2 |

**Rebate schedule (applies retroactively to all units purchased in Year 1):**

| Total annual volume purchased | Rebate on all units |
|---|---|
| 10,000 units or fewer | 0% |
| 10,001 – 15,000 units | 2% |
| More than 15,000 units | 5% |

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Quarter 1 Deliveries and Management's Volume Assessment
exhibits.content:
**Deliveries to Bryce Manufacturing Corp., quarter ended March 31, Year 1 (all invoiced at $50 per unit):**

| Month | Units delivered |
|---|---|
| January | 1,300 |
| February | 1,250 |
| March | 1,450 |
| **Total** | **4,000** |

**Management's probability assessment of Bryce's total Year 1 purchase volume:**

| Annual volume outcome | Rebate rate | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 10,000 units or fewer | 0% | 10% |
| 10,001 – 15,000 units | 2% | 50% |
| More than 15,000 units | 5% | 40% |

Management has concluded that the expected value method better predicts the amount of consideration to which Crestline will be entitled, and that recognizing revenue based on this estimate will not result in a probable significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: March Year 1 Sales to Distributors
exhibits.content:
**March Year 1 sales to independent distributors (control transfers on delivery; all sales on account):**

| Product | Units sold | Selling price per unit | Cost per unit | Return rights |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model X tool kit | 1,000 | $80 | $48 | 60-day unconditional right of return |
| Model Y workbench | 300 | $60 | $35 | None |

Based on more than ten years of experience with similar products, Crestline estimates that 5% of the Model X units sold will be returned. Returned units are expected to be in resalable condition, and the costs of recovering returned units are expected to be negligible. Crestline incurred $1,200 of freight-out on March distributor shipments, which is expensed as incurred. No Model X units had been returned as of March 31, Year 1.

tasks.title: Transaction Price per Unit — Fastener Sales
tasks.instruction: Using the expected value method, compute the transaction price **per unit** for Year 1 fastener sales to Bryce, net of the estimated volume rebate. Enter the amount in dollars and cents (e.g., 48.25), no commas.
tasks.explanation: Under the expected value method, the estimated rebate rate is the probability-weighted average of the possible rebate outcomes: (0% × 10%) + (2% × 50%) + (5% × 40%) = 0% + 1.0% + 2.0% = 3.0%. The estimated rebate per unit is $50 × 3.0% = $1.50, so the transaction price per unit is $50.00 − $1.50 = $48.50. Because the rebate applies retroactively to all units, every unit delivered is recorded at the rebate-adjusted price.
tasks.explanationJa:
期待値法（expected value method）では、起こり得る各リベート率を確率で加重平均して見積ります。

1. 期待リベート率 = (0% × 10%) + (2% × 50%) + (5% × 40%) = 0% + 1.0% + 2.0% = **3.0%**
2. 1個あたりの見積リベート = $50 × 3.0% = **$1.50**
3. 1個あたりの取引価格 = $50.00 − $1.50 = **$48.50**

リベートは年間購入量に応じて**全数量に遡及適用**されるため、引き渡した全ユニットをリベート控除後の単価で収益認識します。

tasks.title: Revenue from Fastener Deliveries — Quarter 1
tasks.instruction: Compute the revenue that Crestline should recognize from fastener deliveries to Bryce for the quarter ended March 31, Year 1 (in whole dollars, no commas).
tasks.explanation: Revenue = units delivered × transaction price per unit = 4,000 units × $48.50 = $194,000. Although Crestline invoices Bryce $200,000 (4,000 × $50), revenue is recognized only for the consideration Crestline expects to be entitled to after the estimated 3% rebate.
tasks.explanationJa:
第1四半期の収益 = 引渡数量 × 1個あたり取引価格で計算します。

1. 引渡数量 = 1,300 + 1,250 + 1,450 = **4,000個**
2. 収益 = 4,000個 × $48.50 = **$194,000**

請求額は 4,000個 × $50 = $200,000 ですが、収益はリベート見積り（3%）控除後の「権利を得ると見込む対価」の金額で認識します。

tasks.title: Refund Liability for Volume Rebates
tasks.instruction: Compute the liability for estimated volume rebates that Crestline should report at March 31, Year 1, related to the fastener deliveries (in whole dollars, no commas).
tasks.explanation: The refund liability equals the consideration invoiced (or received) that Crestline does not expect to be entitled to keep: 4,000 units × $50 × 3.0% = $6,000. Equivalently, amount invoiced $200,000 − revenue recognized $194,000 = $6,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
返金負債（refund liability）は、請求済みの対価のうち顧客に返金すると見込む部分です。

- 計算1: 4,000個 × $50 × 3.0% = **$6,000**
- 計算2（検算）: 請求額 $200,000 − 認識収益 $194,000 = **$6,000**

両方の計算が一致することを確認してください。

tasks.title: Classification of the Rebate Obligation
tasks.instruction: Crestline invoices Bryce $50.00 per unit but recognizes revenue of $48.50 per unit. Select the balance sheet classification that best describes Crestline's obligation for the estimated volume rebates.
options: Valuation allowance deducted from accounts receivable
tasks.explanation: An entity that receives (or has an unconditional right to) consideration it expects to refund to the customer recognizes a refund liability, measured at the amount of consideration the entity does not expect to be entitled to. The rebate obligation is not a contract liability because a contract liability represents an obligation to transfer additional goods or services for consideration already received; here, Crestline's obligation is to return cash, not to perform.
tasks.explanationJa:
見積リベート $6,000 は**返金負債（refund liability）**として表示します。

- **返金負債**: 受け取った（または請求した）対価のうち顧客へ返金すると見込む金額。本問のリベートはこれに該当します（ASC 606-10-32-10）。
- **契約負債（contract liability）**でない理由: 契約負債は「受領済み対価と交換に、追加の財・サービスを移転する義務」を表します。リベートは現金を返す義務であり、履行義務ではありません。
- **契約資産**は企業側の権利（対価に対する条件付きの権利）であり、義務ではないため該当しません。

tasks.title: Revenue from Model X Sales with a Right of Return
tasks.instruction: Compute the sales revenue that Crestline should recognize for March Year 1 from the Model X tool kit sales, after considering expected returns (in whole dollars, no commas).
tasks.explanation: For sales with a right of return, revenue is recognized only for the products not expected to be returned. Expected returns = 1,000 units × 5% = 50 units. Revenue = (1,000 − 50) units × $80 = 950 × $80 = $76,000. The remaining $4,000 (50 units × $80) is recorded as a refund liability.
tasks.explanationJa:
返品権付き販売では、**返品されないと見込む分だけ**収益を認識します。

1. 見積返品数量 = 1,000個 × 5% = **50個**
2. 収益 = (1,000 − 50)個 × $80 = 950個 × $80 = **$76,000**
3. 残りの 50個 × $80 = $4,000 は返金負債として計上します。

なお、Model Y（返品権なし・300個 × $60）はこのタスクの対象外です。設問はModel Xのみを問うています。

tasks.title: Journal Entry — Model X Sales and Cost of Sales
tasks.instruction: Prepare the summary journal entry to record the March Year 1 sales of Model X tool kits, including the related cost of sales and the right-of-return effects. Enter each amount in whole dollars, no commas. Enter 0 in cells that should have no amount.
tasks.explanation: Revenue side: debit Accounts receivable $80,000 (1,000 × $80, the full invoiced amount); credit Sales revenue $76,000 (950 × $80) and credit Refund liability $4,000 (50 × $80). Cost side: total inventory relieved is 1,000 × $48 = $48,000 (credit Inventory); debit Cost of goods sold $45,600 (950 × $48) for the units not expected to be returned, and debit Return asset $2,400 (50 × $48) for the right to recover products from customers. Both sides balance: debits $80,000 + $45,600 + $2,400 = $128,000 = credits $76,000 + $4,000 + $48,000.

tasks.title: Research — Methods for Estimating Variable Consideration
tasks.instruction: Crestline's controller asks you to locate the authoritative guidance that specifies the two methods an entity may use to estimate variable consideration (the expected value method and the most likely amount method). Cite the ASC reference in XXX-XX-XX-XX format.
tasks.explanation: ASC 606-10-32-8 states that an entity shall estimate the amount of variable consideration by using either the expected value method (the sum of probability-weighted amounts in a range of possible outcomes) or the most likely amount method (the single most likely outcome), whichever better predicts the amount of consideration to which the entity will be entitled.
tasks.explanationJa:
変動対価の見積方法（期待値法と最頻値法）を規定しているのは **ASC 606-10-32-8** です。

- **期待値法（expected value）**: 起こり得る結果を確率で加重平均した合計。類似の契約が多数ある場合などに適切。
- **最頻値法（most likely amount）**: 最も可能性の高い単一の金額。結果が2択（達成/未達成）の場合などに適切。

企業は、権利を得ることになる対価をより適切に予測できる方の方法を選択します。

subject: FAR
title: ASC 606: Transaction Price, Allocation, and Contract Balances
scenario:
Vantage Systems Inc. is a calendar-year entity that sells network hardware together with installation and technical support services. On October 1, Year 5 Vantage entered into a contract with Halcyon Corp.

**Exhibit 1** sets out the terms of the contract, **Exhibit 2** provides the standalone selling prices of the promised goods and services, and **Exhibit 3** summarizes the amounts recorded through December 31, Year 5. Vantage has concluded that the hardware, the installation services, and the technical support are each a separate performance obligation.

Determine the amounts Vantage should report for the year ended December 31, Year 5. Ignore income taxes.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Contract with Halcyon Corp — Terms
exhibits.content:
Contract signed October 1, Year 5. Vantage promises to:

1. Deliver 40 network appliances. Control transferred to Halcyon on **November 15, Year 5**.
2. Install and configure the appliances. The installation was **completed December 1, Year 5**. The installation does not significantly modify or customize the hardware.
3. Provide technical support for **24 months beginning December 1, Year 5**. Vantage transfers control of this service evenly over the support period.

**Consideration**

- Fixed consideration of **$960,000**, payable as follows: **$500,000 was paid by Halcyon on November 1, Year 5**; the remaining **$460,000 becomes payable only after Vantage completes the first 12 months of technical support (November 30, Year 6)**.
- A **performance bonus of $120,000** is payable at the end of the 24-month support period if the **integrated system meets the contractual acceptance standards**. Those standards are assessed for the arrangement as a whole and measure the delivered hardware's performance against specification, the completeness and quality of the installation, and the responsiveness of technical support over the support period. Satisfaction of all three performance obligations contributes to meeting the standards, and the bonus is not attributable to any one of them. There are only two possible outcomes: the bonus is earned in full or it is not earned. Management assesses the probability that the acceptance standards will be met at **80%** and has concluded that it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur.
- Vantage will provide Halcyon a **$40,000 cooperative advertising allowance**, settled by reducing the final payment. Vantage does not receive a distinct good or service in exchange for the allowance.

**Other information**

- The contract does not contain a significant financing component; the payment schedule reflects industry practice.
- Vantage paid a $30,000 sales commission to obtain the contract, which it capitalized as a contract cost asset.
- The hardware delivered cost Vantage $420,000.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Standalone Selling Prices
exhibits.content:
Vantage regularly sells each of the following separately at the prices shown.

| Performance obligation | Standalone selling price |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | $700,000 |
| Installation | $140,000 |
| Technical support | $460,000 |
| **Total** | **$1,300,000** |

A competitor publicly quotes $690,000 for comparable hardware and $475,000 for a comparable 24-month support arrangement.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Amounts Recorded Through December 31, Year 5
exhibits.content:
- Cash received from Halcyon through December 31, Year 5: **$500,000** (received November 1, Year 5).
- Amounts billed to Halcyon through December 31, Year 5: **none**.
- Revenue recorded on the contract through December 31, Year 5: **none**. Vantage has deferred all recognition pending completion of this analysis.
- The cooperative advertising allowance has not yet been settled at December 31, Year 5.

tasks.title: Transaction Price
tasks.instruction: Determine the transaction price of the Halcyon contract at December 31, Year 5. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: The transaction price is the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled, adjusted for variable consideration and for consideration payable to a customer. The fixed consideration is $960,000. The performance bonus is variable consideration; because there are only two possible outcomes, the most likely amount is the better predictor, and the most likely outcome is that the bonus is earned, so $120,000 is added. Because it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur, no amount is constrained. The $40,000 cooperative advertising allowance is consideration payable to a customer for which Vantage receives no distinct good or service, so it reduces the transaction price. Transaction price = 960,000 + 120,000 - 40,000 = $1,040,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
取引価格 = 企業が権利を得ると見込む対価。変動対価と顧客に支払う対価を反映させる。

| 構成要素 | 金額 |
| --- | --- |
| 固定対価 | 960,000 |
| 業績ボーナス（変動対価） | +120,000 |
| 協賛広告アローワンス（顧客に支払う対価） | −40,000 |
| **取引価格** | **1,040,000** |

**変動対価の見積り**: 結果が「獲得する／しない」の2通りしかないため **most likely amount（最頻値法）** が適切。80%の確率で獲得と見込むため全額 120,000 を含める。累積収益の重大な戻入れが生じない可能性が高い（probable）ため、制限（constraint）による減額はしない。

**顧客に支払う対価**: 独立した財・サービスの対価でないため収益の減額として取引価格から控除する。

tasks.title: Allocation of the Transaction Price
tasks.instruction: Allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation using the relative standalone selling prices in Exhibit 2. Enter each amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: The transaction price is allocated to each performance obligation in proportion to its standalone selling price. Total standalone selling prices are $1,300,000, so each obligation receives 1,040,000 / 1,300,000 = 80% of its standalone selling price. Hardware: 700,000 x 80% = $560,000. Installation: 140,000 x 80% = $112,000. Technical support: 460,000 x 80% = $368,000. The allocated amounts total $1,040,000. Before applying the proportional method, the exception for allocating variable consideration to a single performance obligation must be considered. That exception applies only when the variable payment terms relate specifically to the entity's efforts to satisfy one performance obligation, or to a specific outcome of satisfying it, and allocating the entire amount to that obligation is consistent with the allocation objective. Here the bonus depends on acceptance standards assessed for the arrangement as a whole, to which the hardware, the installation, and the support all contribute, so it does not relate specifically to any single performance obligation and the exception does not apply. The $120,000 is therefore included in the amount allocated proportionately. The competitor's quoted prices are not used because Vantage has observable standalone selling prices of its own.
tasks.explanationJa:
取引価格は各履行義務の**独立販売価格の比率**で配分する。

配分率 = 取引価格 ÷ 独立販売価格合計 = 1,040,000 ÷ 1,300,000 = **80%**

| 履行義務 | 独立販売価格 | 配分額 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ハードウェア | 700,000 | 700,000 × 80% = **560,000** |
| 据付 | 140,000 | 140,000 × 80% = **112,000** |
| 技術サポート | 460,000 | 460,000 × 80% = **368,000** |
| 合計 | 1,300,000 | **1,040,000** |

**比例配分の前に「特定の履行義務への配分」の例外を検討する**

変動対価は、次の2要件を**両方**満たす場合に限り、特定の履行義務（または区別できる財・サービス）に**全額を配分**しなければならない。

1. 変動的な支払条件が、その履行義務を充足するための企業の努力、またはその充足による**特定の成果**に個別に関連していること
2. 全額をその履行義務に配分することが、配分目的（企業が権利を得ると見込む対価を各履行義務に描写すること）と整合すること

本問のボーナスは、ハードウェアの性能・据付の品質・サポートの対応力を合わせた**統合システム全体の受入基準**に紐づいており、いずれか一つの履行義務に個別に関連するものではない。したがって要件1を満たさず例外は適用できず、$120,000 を含めた取引価格全体を独立販売価格比で比例配分する。

もしボーナスがサポートの成果のみに紐づいていれば、全額を技術サポートに配分することになる。この判断の分岐が得点差になりやすい。

なお、自社に観察可能な独立販売価格があるため、競合他社の提示価格は使用しない。

tasks.title: Revenue Recognized in Year 5
tasks.instruction: Determine the total revenue Vantage should recognize on the Halcyon contract for the year ended December 31, Year 5. Round to the nearest whole dollar and enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Revenue is recognized when each performance obligation is satisfied. The hardware is satisfied at a point in time when control transferred on November 15, Year 5, so $560,000 is recognized. The installation was completed December 1, Year 5, so $112,000 is recognized. The technical support is satisfied over time evenly across 24 months beginning December 1, Year 5, so one month is earned in Year 5: 368,000 x 1/24 = $15,333. Total Year 5 revenue = 560,000 + 112,000 + 15,333 = $687,333.
tasks.explanationJa:
各履行義務の充足時点で収益を認識する。

| 履行義務 | 充足 | Year 5 認識額 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ハードウェア | 11/15 に支配移転（一時点） | 560,000 |
| 据付 | 12/1 に完了（一時点） | 112,000 |
| 技術サポート | 12/1 開始の24ヶ月にわたり均等（一定期間） | 368,000 × 1/24 = 15,333 |
| **合計** | | **687,333** |

サポートは Year 5 中に **1ヶ月分（12月分）**しか経過していない点に注意する。

tasks.title: Contract Asset at December 31, Year 5
tasks.instruction: Determine the contract asset that Vantage should report at December 31, Year 5. Round to the nearest whole dollar and enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: A contract asset arises when an entity has satisfied a performance obligation but its right to consideration is conditional on something other than the passage of time. Revenue recognized through December 31, Year 5 is $687,333, while consideration received is $500,000 and nothing has been billed. The remaining $460,000 becomes payable only after Vantage completes 12 months of support, and the bonus depends on meeting the acceptance standards, so neither is an unconditional right to consideration. Contract asset = 687,333 - 500,000 = $187,333.
tasks.explanationJa:
**契約資産**は、履行義務を充足したが対価を受け取る権利が「時の経過以外の条件」に依存している場合に生じる。

認識済み収益 687,333 − 受領済み対価 500,000 = **$187,333**

残額 $460,000 はサポート12ヶ月完了後でなければ請求できず、ボーナス $120,000 も受入基準の達成が条件のため、いずれも**無条件の権利（受取債権）ではない**。したがって差額は受取債権ではなく契約資産として表示する。

もし受領額が認識済み収益を上回っていれば、逆に契約負債を計上することになる。

tasks.title: Method for Estimating the Performance Bonus
tasks.instruction: Select the method that better predicts the amount of consideration to which Vantage will be entitled for the $120,000 performance bonus described in Exhibit 1.
tasks.explanation: Variable consideration is estimated using either the expected value or the most likely amount, whichever better predicts the amount to which the entity will be entitled. The most likely amount is appropriate when the contract has only two possible outcomes, which is the case here because the bonus is either earned in full or not earned at all. The expected value, a probability-weighted sum, is better suited to contracts with a large number of possible outcomes. The residual approach and the adjusted market assessment approach are methods of estimating a standalone selling price, not variable consideration.
tasks.explanationJa:
変動対価は **expected value（期待値法）** と **most likely amount（最頻値法）** のうち、権利を得る金額をより適切に予測する方法で見積もる。

- **最頻値法**: 起こり得る結果が**2つしかない**契約に適する → 本問はボーナスを「全額獲得する／しない」の2択のため該当
- **期待値法**: 起こり得る結果が**多数ある**契約に適する（確率加重平均）

残余アプローチ（residual approach）と調整済市場評価アプローチ（adjusted market assessment approach）は**独立販売価格**の見積方法であり、変動対価の見積方法ではない。

tasks.title: Support Revenue in Year 6
tasks.instruction: Determine the revenue Vantage will recognize on the technical support performance obligation for the year ended December 31, Year 6, assuming the estimate of the transaction price does not change. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: The technical support is satisfied evenly over the 24-month period that began December 1, Year 5, so 12 of the 24 months fall in Year 6. Revenue = 368,000 x 12/24 = $184,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
技術サポートは Year 5 の12月1日から24ヶ月にわたり均等に充足される。Year 6 には **12ヶ月分**が属する。

368,000 × 12/24 = **$184,000**

（残りの11ヶ月分 368,000 × 11/24 = $168,667 は Year 7 に認識される。1 + 12 + 11 = 24ヶ月で整合する。）

tasks.title: Research: Allocating the Transaction Price
tasks.instruction: Cite the FASB Accounting Standards Codification paragraph that requires an entity to allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation on a relative standalone selling price basis. Cite the ASC reference in XXX-XX-XX-XX format.
tasks.explanation: ASC 606-10-32-31 requires an entity to allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation identified in the contract on a relative standalone selling price basis, except for the specified exceptions for discounts and variable consideration.
tasks.explanationJa:
ASC 606-10-32-31 は、取引価格を契約で識別された各履行義務に**独立販売価格の比率**で配分することを求めている。

例外として、値引きの配分（ASC 606-10-32-36以降）と変動対価の配分（ASC 606-10-32-39以降）について別途の定めがあるが、本問はいずれにも該当しないため原則どおり比例配分する。
